questions.prompt: To which Clan of Quraish Hazrat Umer (RA) belongs?
questions.explanation: Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) belonged to Banu Adi of Quraysh; Abu Bakr (RA) was from Banu Taym and Uthman (RA) from Banu Umayya.

questions.prompt: Author of the book Al-Hisbah fil Islam is:
questions.explanation: Al-Hisbah fi al-Islam, on the office of public accountability (muhtasib), was written by Ibn Taymiyyah.

questions.prompt: How many heads of Zakat are mentioned in Quran?
questions.explanation: Surah al-Tawbah 9:60 names eight categories: the poor, the needy, zakat collectors, those whose hearts are to be won, freeing captives, debtors, in the way of Allah, and wayfarers.

questions.prompt: Hadith which is directly narrated by Tabi is called:
questions.explanation: A mursal hadith is one a Tabi’i attributes directly to the Prophet ﷺ without naming the Companion in between.

questions.prompt: Do not raise your voice above the voice of the Prophet (ﷺ). This order is in Surah?
questions.explanation: Al-Hujurat 49:2: "O you who believe, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet."

questions.prompt: Original name of the host of Holy Prophet(ﷺ), Abu Ayub Ansari (RA) is:
questions.explanation: Abu Ayyub al-Ansari (RA), who hosted the Prophet ﷺ on arrival in Madinah, was named Khalid bin Zayd.

questions.prompt: Tarjman Al-Qur'an is the title of Companion:
questions.explanation: Abdullah ibn Abbas (RA), for whom the Prophet ﷺ prayed for understanding of the Qur’an, is called Tarjuman al-Qur’an.

questions.prompt: Istishab is the term of :
questions.explanation: Istishab (presumption of continuity) is a principle of usul al-fiqh: a ruling continues until evidence changes it.

questions.prompt: For how many years were the Muslims imprisoned in Sha`b Abi Talib in Makkah?
questions.explanation: Quraysh boycotted Banu Hashim, who were confined in Shi’b Abi Talib for about three years (c. 7th–10th year of Prophethood).

questions.prompt: Sahifa-e-Hammam bin Manbah is contained in their entirety in which book?
questions.explanation: The Sahifa of Hammam ibn Munabbih (from Abu Hurayrah RA) is reproduced in full in Musnad Ahmad ibn Hanbal.

questions.prompt: The name of Hazrat Zaid bin Haritha is mentioned in which Surah?
questions.explanation: Zayd (RA) is the only Companion named in the Qur’an, in Al-Ahzab 33:37.

questions.prompt: How many Surahs are there on the name of the Prophets:
questions.explanation: Six surahs are named after prophets: Yunus (10), Hud (11), Yusuf (12), Ibrahim (14), Muhammad (47) and Nuh (71).

questions.prompt: Which Caliph was the first to set the prescribed punishment of drinking at eighty lashes?
questions.explanation: Umar (RA), after consulting the Companions, fixed the punishment for drinking at eighty lashes (Sahih Muslim, Kitab al-Hudud); earlier it was about forty.

questions.prompt: Imam Muslim Bin Hijaj Qusheri died in:
questions.explanation: Imam Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj, compiler of Sahih Muslim, died in Nishapur in 261 AH (875 CE).

questions.prompt: Which Imam has been more extensive in the use of Masal-e-Mursala?
questions.explanation: Al-masalih al-mursalah (unrestricted public interest) is most associated with Imam Malik and the Maliki school.

questions.prompt: "Mujadid-Alf-Thani" is the title of:
questions.explanation: Shaykh Ahmad Sirhindi (1564–1624), the Naqshbandi reformer who opposed Akbar’s Din-i-Ilahi, is called Mujaddid Alf Thani ("reviver of the second millennium").

questions.prompt: The Quranic term "Gharmin" means:
questions.explanation: Al-gharimin (9:60) are people burdened with debt; they are one of the eight recipients of zakat.

questions.prompt: Which event was called Fateh Mubeen (Clear Victory) in the Holy Qur'an?
questions.explanation: Surah al-Fath (48:1), "Indeed We have given you a clear victory," was revealed on the return from the Treaty of Hudaybiyah (6 AH).

questions.prompt: If the husband is childless, how much does the widow get from the husband's inheritance?
questions.explanation: Al-Nisa 4:12: wives get one-fourth if the husband leaves no child, and one-eighth if he does.

questions.prompt: Ghazwa Khandaq is called as:
questions.explanation: The Battle of the Trench (5 AH) is also called Ghazwa al-Ahzab (the Confederates), the subject of Surah al-Ahzab; Yawm al-Furqan refers to Badr.

questions.prompt: Abdullah bin Salam (RA) was _________ before accepting Islam.
questions.explanation: Abdullah ibn Salam (RA) was a Jewish rabbi of Madinah (Banu Qaynuqa) before Islam, so none of the options is correct.

questions.prompt: Zainab bint Khuzaima (may Allah be pleased with her) belonged to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ as:
questions.explanation: Zaynab bint Khuzaymah (RA), called Umm al-Masakin (mother of the poor), married the Prophet ﷺ and died a few months later.

questions.prompt: At what time is the Kusoof prayer performed?
questions.explanation: Salat al-Kusuf is offered during a solar eclipse; the prayer for a lunar eclipse is Salat al-Khusuf.

questions.prompt: Hudaybiyyah peace document was written from Muslims side by:
questions.explanation: Ali ibn Abi Talib (RA) wrote the Treaty of Hudaybiyah (Sahih Bukhari, Kitab al-Sulh).

questions.prompt: Among the Ummahat ul Momineen (mothers of the believers) is:
questions.explanation: None of them was a wife of the Prophet ﷺ; Umm Hani was his cousin (daughter of Abu Talib).

questions.prompt: Hadith Taqreeri mentions:
options: The speeches of the Messenger of Allah
The silence of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the work of a companion
questions.explanation: A taqriri hadith records the Prophet’s ﷺ tacit approval: an act done in his presence that he did not object to.

questions.prompt: The basic obligatory action of Hajj is:
questions.explanation: Standing at Arafah on 9 Dhul Hijjah is the essential pillar of Hajj: "Hajj is Arafah" (Tirmidhi, Abu Dawud).

questions.prompt: Dare Arqam was located in:
questions.explanation: Dar al-Arqam, the early meeting place of the Muslims, was in Makkah near Mount Safa, so none of the options is right.

questions.prompt: To whom did Haroon Al-Rashid give the responsibility of writing a book on finance?
questions.explanation: Qadi Abu Yusuf, Abu Hanifa’s student, wrote Kitab al-Kharaj on public finance and taxation for Harun al-Rashid.

questions.prompt: The author of Kitab al-Hind is:
questions.explanation: Abu Rayhan al-Biruni wrote Kitab al-Hind (c. 1030); Abu al-Fazl wrote the Akbarnama.

questions.prompt: Sheikh Ali Hajwiri came to Lahore during whose period?
questions.explanation: Ali Hujwiri (Data Ganj Bakhsh) reached Lahore around 1039–41 CE, in the reign of Sultan Mas’ud Ghaznavi (r. 1030–41), son of Mahmud.

questions.prompt: Who was the first to treat Hindus as people of the book in his time?
questions.explanation: After conquering Sindh (712 CE), Muhammad bin Qasim gave Hindus and Buddhists protected dhimmi status like the People of the Book, on payment of jizya.

questions.prompt: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood in respect for the funeral of a:
questions.explanation: Sahih Bukhari 1312: the Prophet ﷺ stood for a Jew’s funeral and said, "Is it not a human soul?"

questions.prompt: Shaykh Ahmad Sirhandi's line of Sufism was:
questions.explanation: Shaykh Ahmad Sirhindi belonged to the Naqshbandi order (founding the Mujaddidi branch), which is not among the options.

questions.prompt: During whose rule the subcontinent had 25% of the world's total GDP?
questions.explanation: Angus Maddison estimated Mughal India’s share of world GDP at about 24–25% around 1700, in Aurangzeb’s reign.

questions.prompt: The aim of the Silk Handkerchief Movement was to achieve freedom of which country?
questions.explanation: The Silk Letter Movement (1913–20), led by Deobandi scholars under Mahmud al-Hasan, aimed to free India from British rule with Ottoman and Afghan help.

questions.prompt: ___________ is called the New Testament.
questions.explanation: The Injil (Gospel) given to Isa (AS) corresponds to the New Testament; the Torah and Psalms (Zabur) are in the Old Testament.

questions.prompt: Who is the author of the book “The Reconstruction of Religious Thought in Islam”?
questions.explanation: The Reconstruction of Religious Thought in Islam (1930/1934) is Allama Muhammad Iqbal’s collection of lectures.

questions.prompt: According to the MUFASSIRIN, what is meant by 'فی سبیل اللہ' in the heads of Zakat?
questions.explanation: Most classical exegetes take fi sabilillah in 9:60 to mean those striving in jihad (fighters for Allah’s cause).

questions.prompt: Who is the author of the book on Seerah titled 'Khutbat-e-Madras'?
questions.explanation: Khutbat-e-Madras is the collection of eight lectures on the Seerah that Syed Sulaiman Nadvi gave in Madras in 1925.

questions.prompt: According to which Surah, the killing of one human being is equal to the killing of all mankind ?
questions.explanation: Al-Ma’idah 5:32: whoever kills a soul unjustly, it is as if he had killed all mankind.

questions.prompt: Who is the author of 'The Clash of Civilizations'?
questions.explanation: Samuel P. Huntington set out the Clash of Civilizations thesis in a 1993 article and a 1996 book.

questions.prompt: Which Islamic organization was established in the year 1969 ?
questions.explanation: The OIC was founded at the Rabat summit in September 1969 after the arson at Al-Aqsa; the Arab League dates from 1945 and the PLO from 1964.

questions.prompt: In which school of thought is the principle of 'ISTEHSAN' most extensively applied ?
questions.explanation: Istihsan (juristic preference) is most associated with the Hanafi school, which is not listed; Imam Shafi’i rejected it.

questions.prompt: Polygamy is allowed for a man under which condition?
questions.explanation: Al-Nisa 4:3 allows up to four wives but adds, "if you fear you will not be just, then only one".

questions.prompt: In the final major address to the Ummah, what type of equality did the Prophet ﷺ emphasize?
questions.explanation: The Farewell Sermon declared that no Arab is superior to a non-Arab, nor white to black, except by piety: the equality of all human beings.

questions.prompt: According to Almighty Allah, what is the basis of being most honored?
questions.explanation: Al-Hujurat 49:13: "the most honoured of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you."

questions.prompt: Which is considered the first battle led by the Prophet (ﷺ) in Islamic history?
questions.explanation: The expedition of Abwa (Waddan), in Safar 2 AH, was the first ghazwa the Prophet ﷺ led in person; no fighting took place. Badr came later that year.

questions.prompt: When one person provides capital and the other provides labor and both share profit and loss, what is it called?
questions.explanation: In mudarabah one party (rabb al-mal) gives capital and the other (mudarib) gives work; profit is shared as agreed, and financial loss falls on the capital provider.

questions.prompt: What was the common central point of the message of all the Prophets?
questions.explanation: Al-Nahl 16:36 and Al-Anbiya 21:25: every messenger was sent with the message to worship Allah alone (tawhid).

questions.prompt: How many basic conditions are required for a Hadith to be regarded as authentic?
questions.explanation: A sahih hadith needs five conditions: a continuous chain, upright narrators, precise narrators, no shudhudh (irregularity) and no hidden defect (illah).

questions.prompt: The first verses of the Qur'an revealed to the Prophet (PBUH) in the Cave of Hira were from Surah:
questions.explanation: Al-Alaq 96:1–5 ('Read in the name of your Lord who created') was the first revelation.

questions.prompt: The shortest surah of the Qur'an is:
questions.explanation: Al-Kawthar (108) has three ayat.

questions.prompt: Which surah does not begin with Bismillah?
questions.explanation: Surah 9, At-Tawbah (Bara'ah), begins without Bismillah.

questions.prompt: In which surah does Bismillah appear twice, once at the start and once within the text?
questions.explanation: An-Naml 27:30 contains Bismillah in Sulaiman's letter to the Queen of Sheba.

questions.prompt: The only surah named after a woman is:
questions.explanation: Surah 19 is named after Maryam, mother of Isa (AS); she is the only woman named in the Qur'an.

questions.prompt: Ayat al-Kursi is verse number ____ of Surah Al-Baqarah.
questions.explanation: Al-Baqarah 2:255 describes Allah's sovereignty and knowledge.

questions.prompt: The longest verse of the Qur'an, concerning the recording of debts, is:
questions.explanation: Ayat al-Dayn (2:282) instructs believers to write down loan contracts before witnesses.

questions.prompt: Which surah, according to a hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari, is equal to one-third of the Qur'an?
questions.explanation: Al-Ikhlas (112) sets out pure Tawhid.

questions.prompt: Which surah is called Umm al-Kitab (Mother of the Book)?
questions.explanation: Al-Fatiha is recited in every rak'ah of salah.

questions.prompt: The Qur'an was first compiled into a single written volume during the caliphate of:
questions.explanation: After many huffaz fell at Yamamah, Zaid bin Thabit (RA) compiled it at Umar's suggestion.

questions.prompt: Who led the task of compiling the Qur'an under Abu Bakr (RA) and the standard copies under Uthman (RA)?
questions.explanation: Zaid bin Thabit, a scribe of revelation, led both efforts.

questions.prompt: The compiled copy of the Qur'an prepared under Abu Bakr (RA) was later kept with:
questions.explanation: Uthman (RA) borrowed Hafsa's copy to prepare the standard copies.

questions.prompt: How many prophets are mentioned by name in the Qur'an?
questions.explanation: Twenty-five prophets are named, from Adam to Muhammad (PBUH).

questions.prompt: The prophet mentioned by name most often in the Qur'an is:
questions.explanation: Musa (AS) is mentioned more than 130 times.

questions.prompt: The verse 'This day I have perfected your religion for you' (Al-Ma'idah 5:3) was revealed:
options: at Arafat during the Farewell Pilgrimage
questions.explanation: It was revealed on the Day of Arafah, 10 AH.

questions.prompt: The journey of Isra from Masjid al-Haram to Masjid al-Aqsa is mentioned in:
questions.explanation: Surah Al-Isra (Bani Isra'il) opens with the Night Journey.

questions.prompt: The change of qiblah from Bait al-Maqdis to the Ka'bah is commanded in:
questions.explanation: The qiblah changed in 2 AH, about 16–17 months after the Hijrah.

questions.prompt: 'There is no compulsion in religion' is stated in:
questions.explanation: The verse immediately follows Ayat al-Kursi.

questions.prompt: The verse 'whoever kills a soul... it is as if he had slain mankind entirely' is:
questions.explanation: It stresses the sanctity of human life.

questions.prompt: Surah Al-Hujurat 49:13 states that Allah made people into nations and tribes so that they may:
questions.explanation: The noblest in Allah's sight is the most righteous (taqwa).

questions.prompt: The prohibition of backbiting is compared to eating the flesh of one's dead brother in:
questions.explanation: 49:12 forbids suspicion, spying and backbiting.

questions.prompt: The final verses prohibiting intoxicants and gambling, calling them 'the work of Satan', are:
questions.explanation: The prohibition came in stages: 2:219, 4:43 and finally 5:90–91.

questions.prompt: Which surah of the Qur'an is named after a prophet who was swallowed by a fish?
questions.explanation: Yunus (AS) is also called Dhun-Nun; Surah 10 bears his name.

questions.prompt: The story described in the Qur'an as 'the best of stories' (ahsan al-qasas) is that of:
questions.explanation: Yusuf 12:3; the whole of Surah 12 narrates his story.

questions.prompt: The Qur'an describes the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) as 'Khatam an-Nabiyyin' (Seal of the Prophets) in:
questions.explanation: This verse is the basis of the finality of prophethood.

questions.prompt: Surah Al-Fil (105) refers to the event that took place in the year of the Prophet's birth, when an army attacked the Ka'bah led by:
questions.explanation: The Year of the Elephant is about 570 CE.

questions.prompt: The command to obey parents and never say 'uff' to them is in:
questions.explanation: 17:23 links worship of Allah alone with kindness to parents.

questions.prompt: Sahih al-Bukhari was compiled by:
questions.explanation: Al-Bukhari (d. 256 AH) is regarded as the most authentic hadith collection.

questions.prompt: Which of these is NOT one of the six major Sunni hadith collections (Sihah Sitta)?
questions.explanation: The six are Bukhari, Muslim, Abu Dawud, Tirmidhi, Nasa'i and Ibn Majah.

questions.prompt: The four primary sources of Islamic law, in order, are:
questions.explanation: Ijma is consensus of scholars; Qiyas is analogical reasoning.

questions.prompt: The hadith 'Actions are judged by intentions' is narrated by:
questions.explanation: It opens Sahih al-Bukhari.

questions.prompt: A hadith whose words are from Allah but expressed by the Prophet (PBUH) is called:
questions.explanation: Hadith Qudsi conveys Allah's meaning in the Prophet's words; it is not part of the Qur'an.

questions.prompt: A hadith reported by so many narrators at every stage that agreement on a falsehood is inconceivable is called:
questions.explanation: Mutawatir reports give certain knowledge; ahad reports are those that fall short of this.

questions.prompt: Musnad, one of the largest hadith collections arranged by Companion narrators, was compiled by:
questions.explanation: It is arranged by the Companion who narrated each hadith rather than by subject.

questions.prompt: The angel who will blow the trumpet (Sur) on the Day of Judgement is:
questions.explanation: The first blast ends life on earth; the second begins the resurrection.

questions.prompt: The angels who question the dead in the grave are:
questions.explanation: Kiraman Katibin are the noble recorders of deeds.

questions.prompt: The Zabur was revealed to:
questions.explanation: Tawrat was given to Musa, Zabur to Dawud, Injil to Isa and the Qur'an to Muhammad (PBUH).

questions.prompt: The Qur'an mentions the 'Suhuf' (scriptures) of Ibrahim and Musa in:
questions.explanation: 87:18–19: 'This is in the former scriptures, the scriptures of Ibrahim and Musa.'

questions.prompt: Belief in Al-Qadr means belief in:
options: divine decree: Allah's knowledge and ordaining of all things
the life of the grave only
questions.explanation: Qadr is one of the six articles of faith listed in the Hadith of Jibril (Sahih Muslim).

questions.prompt: The Hadith of Jibril (Sahih Muslim) defines Ihsan as:
options: worshipping Allah as though you see Him
fighting in the way of Allah
questions.explanation: '...and if you do not see Him, He surely sees you.'

questions.prompt: The Qur'anic name for the period between death and resurrection is:
questions.explanation: Al-Mu'minun 23:100 speaks of a barrier (barzakh) until the Day they are raised.

questions.prompt: The five daily prayers were made obligatory on the occasion of:
questions.explanation: They were prescribed during the Night Journey and Ascension, before the Hijrah.

questions.prompt: Fasting in Ramadan was made obligatory in:
questions.explanation: Al-Baqarah 2:183: 'Fasting is prescribed for you...'

questions.prompt: The rate of zakat on savings, gold, silver and trade goods is:
questions.explanation: Zakat is due once a lunar year has passed on wealth at or above the nisab.

questions.prompt: The nisab of zakat for silver is:
questions.explanation: The nisab is 52.5 tolas (about 612 g) of silver or 7.5 tolas (about 87.5 g) of gold.

questions.prompt: The eight categories of recipients of zakat are listed in:
questions.explanation: They include the poor, the needy, zakat collectors, debtors and wayfarers.

questions.prompt: Ushr on produce of land watered by rain or natural sources is:
questions.explanation: Land irrigated by human effort pays half that, 5 percent.

questions.prompt: The essential rite of Hajj without which Hajj is not valid is staying at Arafat on:
questions.explanation: The Prophet (PBUH) said 'Hajj is Arafah' (Tirmidhi).

questions.prompt: The Qur'anic verse making Hajj obligatory on those able to undertake the journey is:
questions.explanation: 3:97: 'Pilgrimage to the House is a duty owed to Allah by people who are able.'

questions.prompt: The method of performing wudu is described in:
questions.explanation: The same verse permits tayammum when water is not available.

questions.prompt: The obligatory charity paid before Eid al-Fitr prayer is called:
questions.explanation: It purifies the fast and helps the poor celebrate Eid.

questions.prompt: The Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) was born in Makkah in the 'Year of the Elephant', about:
questions.explanation: The first revelation came around 610 CE when he was 40.

questions.prompt: The Prophet (PBUH) received the first revelation at the age of:
questions.explanation: He was 25 at his marriage to Khadijah (RA) and 53 at the Hijrah.

questions.prompt: The Prophet's (PBUH) wet-nurse was:
questions.explanation: He spent his early childhood with Halimah among the Banu Sa'd.

questions.prompt: The Prophet's (PBUH) mother, Aminah, died at:
questions.explanation: He was about six years old at the time.

questions.prompt: The Prophet (PBUH) belonged to which clan of the Quraysh?
questions.explanation: His grandfather Abdul Muttalib was chief of Banu Hashim.

questions.prompt: The pact of chivalry the Prophet (PBUH) joined in his youth to help the oppressed is known as:
questions.explanation: He later said he would still answer such a call in Islam.

questions.prompt: The first migration of Muslims to Abyssinia (Habshah) took place in:
questions.explanation: The Negus (Najashi) of Abyssinia gave the emigrants protection.

questions.prompt: The 'Year of Sorrow' (Aam al-Huzn) is the year in which the Prophet (PBUH) lost:
questions.explanation: Both died in the 10th year of prophethood.

questions.prompt: The first mosque built by the Prophet (PBUH) was:
questions.explanation: It was built on arrival at Quba, near Madinah, during the Hijrah.

questions.prompt: The Charter of Madinah (Mithaq al-Madinah) was concluded between:
options: the Muslims, Jewish tribes and other inhabitants of Madinah
the Muslims and the Byzantine Empire
the Muslims and the Quraysh of Makkah
the Ansar and the Muhajirun only
questions.explanation: It is often called the first written constitution of a state.

questions.prompt: The Battle of Badr was fought in:
questions.explanation: About 313 Muslims defeated a much larger Makkan force on 17 Ramadan 2 AH.

questions.prompt: Who suggested digging a trench to defend Madinah in 5 AH?
questions.explanation: The Battle of the Trench (Khandaq) is also called Ahzab.

questions.prompt: The Treaty of Hudaybiyyah, called 'a clear victory' in Surah Al-Fath, was concluded in:
questions.explanation: Al-Fath 48:1 refers to the treaty.

questions.prompt: The Battle of Khaybar took place in:
questions.explanation: Khaybar's fortresses were taken after the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah.

questions.prompt: The Farewell Sermon (Khutbat al-Wada') was delivered at:
questions.explanation: It was delivered on 9 Dhul-Hijjah 10 AH.

questions.prompt: The first muezzin of Islam was:
questions.explanation: Bilal's voice called the first adhan in Madinah.

questions.prompt: The first woman to accept Islam was:
questions.explanation: Khadijah bint Khuwaylid was the Prophet's first wife.

questions.prompt: The first martyr in Islam was:
questions.explanation: She was killed in Makkah by Abu Jahl.

questions.prompt: The first Caliph, Abu Bakr (RA), was given the title:
questions.explanation: He confirmed the Prophet's account of the Mi'raj without hesitation.

questions.prompt: Abu Bakr (RA) fought the Riddah Wars against:
options: apostates and those refusing to pay zakat
questions.explanation: His firm stance preserved the unity of the state after the Prophet's death.

questions.prompt: The Hijri calendar was introduced in the reign of:
questions.explanation: Umar fixed the Hijrah as the starting point, around 17 AH.

questions.prompt: Umar (RA) established the Diwan, which was:
options: a register of soldiers and stipend recipients
questions.explanation: The Diwan system organised payments from the Bait al-Mal.

questions.prompt: Jerusalem was taken peacefully by the Muslims and Umar (RA) travelled there to receive it in:
questions.explanation: The Patriarch Sophronius handed over the city to Umar.

questions.prompt: The Battle of Qadisiyyah (636 CE), which broke Sasanian Persian power, was led by:
questions.explanation: Qadisiyyah opened Iraq to the Muslims.

questions.prompt: The Battle of Yarmouk (636 CE) was fought against the:
questions.explanation: Khalid bin Walid (RA) commanded the Muslim army; Syria passed to the Muslims.

questions.prompt: Uthman (RA) is known as 'Dhun-Nurain' because he:
options: married two daughters of the Prophet (PBUH)
questions.explanation: He married Ruqayyah (RA) and, after her death, Umm Kulthum (RA).

questions.prompt: Copies of the Qur'an in a single standard reading were sent to the provinces by:
questions.explanation: He was given the title Jami' al-Qur'an for this.

questions.prompt: Ali (RA) moved the capital of the caliphate from Madinah to:
questions.explanation: Damascus later became the Umayyad capital; Baghdad was founded by the Abbasids.

questions.prompt: The Companion called 'Amin al-Ummah' (Trustee of the Ummah) is:
questions.explanation: The Prophet (PBUH) gave him this title (Bukhari and Muslim).

questions.prompt: The Bayt al-Hikmah (House of Wisdom), a centre of translation and learning, flourished in:
questions.explanation: It reached its height under Caliph al-Ma'mun in the 9th century.

questions.prompt: The word 'algebra' comes from a book by:
questions.explanation: His 'al-Kitab al-Mukhtasar fi Hisab al-Jabr wal-Muqabala' gave algebra its name.

questions.prompt: 'Al-Qanun fi al-Tibb' (The Canon of Medicine) was written by:
questions.explanation: It was a standard medical textbook in Europe for centuries.

questions.prompt: The 'Muqaddimah', a pioneering work on history and society, was written by:
questions.explanation: It analyses 'asabiyyah (group solidarity) and the rise and fall of dynasties.

questions.prompt: 'Kitab al-Hind', a detailed study of India, was written by:
questions.explanation: Al-Biruni travelled with Mahmud of Ghazni's campaigns.

questions.prompt: Ibn al-Haytham is best known for his work on:
questions.explanation: His Kitab al-Manazir (Book of Optics) explained vision through light entering the eye.

questions.prompt: The physician who first clearly distinguished smallpox from measles was:
questions.explanation: Al-Razi (Rhazes) wrote a treatise on the two diseases.

questions.prompt: 'Kitab al-Tasrif', an illustrated encyclopaedia of surgery, was written by:
questions.explanation: Al-Zahrawi of Cordoba is called the father of surgery.

questions.prompt: The philosopher known in Europe as 'Averroes', famous for commentaries on Aristotle, is:
questions.explanation: Ibn Rushd was a judge and philosopher of Cordoba.

questions.prompt: 'Ihya Ulum al-Din' (The Revival of the Religious Sciences) was written by:
questions.explanation: Al-Ghazali (d. 1111) taught at the Nizamiyya of Baghdad.

questions.prompt: The famous traveller who wrote the 'Rihla' after journeys across Africa and Asia was:
questions.explanation: Ibn Battuta of Tangier travelled for nearly 30 years and visited Sindh and Delhi.

questions.prompt: The Abbasid capital Baghdad was founded in 762 CE by Caliph:
questions.explanation: It was laid out as the Round City (Madinat al-Salam).

questions.prompt: Muhammad bin Qasim conquered Sindh in:
questions.explanation: He took Debal and defeated Raja Dahir.

questions.prompt: Tariq bin Ziyad crossed into Spain (al-Andalus) in:
questions.explanation: Gibraltar (Jabal Tariq) is named after him.

questions.prompt: Salahuddin Ayyubi recaptured Jerusalem in 1187 after the Battle of:
questions.explanation: Ain Jalut (1260) was the Mamluk victory over the Mongols.

questions.prompt: The Dome of the Rock in Jerusalem was built by Umayyad Caliph:
